facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: As a result of your curse, Hari shall assume the form of a rock on the banks of the river Gandaki and shall preside on the same in Bharata.
facts.text: The Shiva Purana recounts that the chaste woman Vrinda cursed Lord Vishnu to become a stone after he deceived her by disguising himself as her husband, the demon king Jalandhara.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: As per a blessing by Vishnu to marry Vrinda in her next birth, Vishnu in form of Shaligram married Tulsi on Prabodhini Ekadashi.
facts.text: The Padma Purana records that the sacred Tulsi plant emerged from the cremation pyre of Vrinda, leading Vishnu to pledge eternal marriage to her in his Shaligram form on Devutthana Ekadashi.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Vishnu, on being cursed by Tulasi, assumed the form of a large rocky mountain known as shaligrama, on the banks of the Gandaki River where vajrakita, a type of worm with teeth as strong as the vajra, carved out various markings on his body.
facts.text: In the Brahmavaivarta Purana, Vishnu instructs that he will reside along the Gandaki River as a stone while celestial insects known as Vajrakita carve auspicious disc marks into his form.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: According to the Devi Bhagavata Purana, Brahmavaivarta Purana, and Shiva Purana, shilagrama shilas originated due to the following chain of events.
facts.text: The Devi Bhagavata Purana states that offering worship to a Shaligram stone is inherently incomplete unless sacred Tulsi leaves are dedicated during the ritual.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: The Garuda Purana details specific physical classifications of Shaligram stones based on the count of concentric chakra circles and their apertural openings.
facts.text: The Garuda Purana catalogues dozens of Shaligram types according to the number, position, and coloration of their circular markings, linking specific forms to deities such as Sudarshana, Narasimha, and Damodara.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: the sacred tulsi plant is annually wedded, often with elaborate ritual and costly feasting, to the Salagrama stone.
facts.source_name: ASI, Mohenjo-Daro and the Indus Civilization
facts.text: In 1931, archaeologist Sir John Marshall recorded during excavations for the Archaeological Survey of India that the sacred Tulsi plant is ceremonially wedded to the Salagrama stone across traditional Indian households.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: a Shivling and one sacred Shaligram stone were found. Later, a team of the Archaeological Survey of India officials reached the site and examined the idols.
facts.text: In June 2022, an excavation examined by officials from the Archaeological Survey of India at Nahabhanga village in Odisha recovered fourteen antique deity idols alongside a sacred Shaligram stone.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: There were 4-5 Saligram over the silver throne.
facts.source_name: Supreme Court of India / ASI Records
facts.text: Official excavation documentation and custodial court inventories recorded five sacred Shaligram stones preserved for worship within the sanctum precinct at the disputed Ayodhya archaeological site.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: On March 6, the Geological Survey of India (GSI) declared Langza a geo-heritage site.
facts.source_name: Geological Survey of India / The Tribune
facts.text: In March 2026, the Geological Survey of India declared the ammonite-bearing Jurassic strata of Langza village in Himachal Pradesh a national geo-heritage site at an elevation of 4,400 metres.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: When the ammonites in the shaligram stones were alive, floating around in the sea, they were at the southern edge of the Neotethys.
facts.text: Geological research confirms that Shaligram stones originating from the Spiti Shales along the Kali Gandaki River are fossilized marine cephalopods from the prehistoric Tethys Ocean dating to roughly 150 million years ago.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Often their existence was explained with myth and religion since the science of palaeontology didn't begin in earnest until around the 18th century.
facts.text: While Puranic mythology attributes the distinctive spiral markings to incisions made by diamond-toothed Vajrakita worms, paleontologists demonstrate that they are the natural septal walls and suture patterns of extinct ammonites.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Through practitioners' radically different ways of viewing personhood and agency, Shaligrams become both fossil and deity in such a way that blends discourses of science and religion into equal parts geology, paleontology, history, spirituality, and mythology.
facts.text: Scholars and geomythologists disagree on whether ancient Vedic practitioners revered Shaligrams due to an intuitive understanding of petrified natural organisms or solely because their geometric whorls matched the sacred iconography of Vishnu's discus.
